study_identification.title: Effects of anterior temporal lobe resection on cortical morphology

study_characteristics.study_objective: To examine the effects of anterior temporal lobe resection (ATLR) surgery on brain morphology in individuals with temporal lobe epilepsy using both traditional and recently-developed independent morphological measures (K, I, S), and to understand the consequences and processes of reorganization following ATLR.

dataset_name.answer: NKI (Nathan Kline Institute); NHNN (National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery); Chalfont Centre for Epilepsy

hc_n.answer: 924 (833 from NKI dataset; 91 matched controls from NHNN/Chalfont: 22 with scanning protocol 1, 69 with scanning protocol 2; 96 NKI subjects rejected due to inadequate image quality and motion artifacts)

hc_age.answer: Data not fully reported in paper; NKI dataset covers entire age range to ensure robust models

preprocessing_pipeline.answer: FreeSurfer 6.0 recon-all pipeline; local gyrification index processing stream; manual correction of grey- and white matter segmentation using control points; surface-based method for local morphological measures

quality_checking_detail.answer: 96 subjects (approximately 9.4%) of the NKI dataset were rejected prior to analysis due to inadequate image quality and motion artifacts. Manual correction of grey- and white matter segmentation performed where necessary. Visual inspection to ensure no distortions to Desikan-Killiany atlas surface ROI labels around the resected area by comparing pre- and postoperative scans.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Generalized additive mixed models (GAMM) using R package mgcv with scanning protocol as random effect. Formula: y ~ s(age) + sex + s(subject, bs='re') + s(scanning_protocol, bs='re'). Site-specific controls matching the patients informed effects for the specific scanning protocols. NKI data used for training to ensure robust models across entire age range; site-specific control data processed without/with temporal lobes for correcting ipsilateral/contralateral sides respectively.

response_variable.answer: Local cortical thickness (T); Local total surface area (At); Local exposed surface area (Ae) - measured in 3cm radius patches around each vertex. Derived independent measures: K (tension/pressure), I (isometric size), S (shape/complexity)

predictor_effects.answer: Age: smooth spline fixed effect s(age); Sex: fixed effect; Scanning protocol: random effect s(scanning_protocol, bs='re'); Subject: random effect s(subject, bs='re'). Restricted maximum likelihood (REML) used for smoothing parameter estimation.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study uses GAMM with random effects for scanning protocol and subject, which addresses some nuisance structure. However, detailed validation metrics for handling nuisance structure (e.g., evaluation of variance homogeneity, correlation structure, nonlinearity handling) are not explicitly reported. The model accounts for age (nonlinear via splines), sex, and scanner/protocol differences (random effects), and manual quality control was performed. Site-specific controls inform protocol-specific effects. However, no explicit metrics like MSLL, skewness/kurtosis of residuals, or formal tests of heteroscedasticity are reported.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: We trained a model with the formula y ~ s(age) + sex + s(subject, bs='re') + s(scanning_protocol, bs='re'), using restricted maximum likelihood as the method for smoothing parameter estimation. We used the controls to provide a normative model of age and sex with scanning protocol as a random effect... The site-specific controls matching the patients then informed effects for the specific scanning protocols.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The paper does not report validation metrics on the training data (healthy controls). No metrics such as explained variance, correlation between predicted and observed values, or residual distributions are provided for the normative model on the control dataset.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: No explicit validation metrics on training data are reported in the main text or supplementary materials.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study does not report hold-out validation or cross-validation on independent healthy control data. All 924 controls appear to be used for training the normative model without reporting independent test set validation metrics.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: No mention of hold-out validation, cross-validation, or independent test set evaluation is found in the methods or results sections.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The normative model trained on healthy controls is applied to TLE patients (different domain), and the study validates that the scaling law holds in TLE patients before surgery. The slopes of cortical folding in TLE patients (mean = 1.246) align with the predicted universal scaling law slope of 1.25, suggesting the normative framework is applicable to this different domain. However, formal quantitative validation metrics (e.g., calibration, prediction intervals) are not reported.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: We first verified that the local folding in individuals with TLE follows the universal scaling law. As shown in Fig. 3, the slopes of each subject's hemispheres are distributed around a mean of 1.246, indicating that the scaling law also applies to our cohort of individuals with TLE... We assessed the fit of the scaling law to the cortical folding of individuals with TLE before surgery by regressing between the quantities log₁₀(Ae') and log₁₀(At'√T) across each hemisphere, and comparing the slope of this regression to the predicted slope of 1.25.

clinical_dataset.answer: NHNN (National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery); Chalfont Centre for Epilepsy

diseases_studied.answer: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) - drug-resistant; undergoing anterior temporal lobe resection (ATLR)

clinical_groups_age.answer: Age range 19-60 years (exact mean and SD not reported for entire cohort)

deviation_metric.answer: Z-score (subject-wise centered pre- to post-operative changes). Morphological changes measured in Cohen's f² effect size. Cluster-wise significance at p ≤ 0.05 using random field theory correction for multiple comparisons.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: SurfStat toolbox (Worsley et al., 2009) for surface-based statistical analysis with random field theory correction for multiple comparisons and spatial correlation. Design matrix with effects for preoperative and postoperative surface groups, using contrast to test differences. Cluster-wise model significance threshold p ≤ 0.05. Effect sizes reported in Cohen's f². Covariate analyses tested for effects of: age at surgery, duration since first seizure, resection volume, side of resection, time between surgery and postoperative scan, and seizure outcome (ILAE 1&2 vs 3+). No significant covariate effects were found at cluster significance of 0.05.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: ATLR causes widespread bilateral morphological changes, mainly ipsilateral (orbitofrontal/inferior frontal gyri, pre-/postcentral gyri, supramarginal gyrus, lateral occipital gyrus, lingual cortex) and some contralateral (lateral occipital gyrus, inferior frontal gyrus, frontal pole), with independent measures K, I, S revealing additional effects not detected by traditional measures.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Widespread morphological changes were observed following ATLR across all six measures studied. Ipsilateral effects included: (1) Orbitofrontal and inferior frontal gyri showed increased total surface area (f²=0.29), increased exposed surface area (f²=0.58), decreased tension K (f²=-2.38), increased isometric term I (f²=0.43), and increased shape complexity S (f²=0.39); (2) Pre- and postcentral gyri and supramarginal gyrus showed increased thickness and increased K; (3) Lateral occipital gyrus and lingual cortex showed decreased thickness (f²=-0.07 to -0.09), decreased exposed area, and increased K. Contralateral effects included: (1) Lateral occipital gyrus showed increased thickness (f²=0.06), increased areas (f²=0.08), and increased K and I (f²=0.07-0.09); (2) Inferior frontal gyrus and frontal pole showed increased areas and K. The scaling law slope in TLE patients (mean=1.246) validated applicability of the framework. No significant effects were found for covariates including age at surgery, TLE duration, resection volume, side of resection, post-surgical interval, or seizure outcome (ILAE classification). Regions affected showed structural connectivity to resected anterior temporal lobe via white matter tracts (uncinate fasciculus, inferior longitudinal fasciculus, inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus), suggesting Wallerian degeneration or compensatory plasticity as potential mechanisms. Independent measures K, I, S detected morphological changes in regions (e.g., supramarginal gyrus, contralateral frontal pole) not identified by traditional measures.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Sample size limitations for detecting onset-side effects despite observed differences between left and right resections. Cannot definitively determine whether morphological changes represent atrophy, reorganization, or compensatory mechanisms without functional correlation studies. Age range limited to 19-60 years; effects outside this range unknown. Lack of data on language lateralization effects. Limited follow-up duration (median 3.6 months, range 2-13 months); longer-term longitudinal studies needed. Insula and corpus callosum regions excluded from analysis due to method limitations in flat or deep sulcal regions. No analysis of morphological changes within the resected ipsilateral temporal lobe itself (excluded from analysis). Temporal resolution insufficient to determine timeline of morphological changes. No functional outcome correlation (language, memory, visual, cognitive) despite known cognitive decline in 25-50% of ATLR patients. Seizure outcome analysis limited by sample size (n=23 with recurrent seizures). Cross-sectional control data rather than longitudinal controls.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: This study primarily uses normative modeling as a methodological tool to correct for healthy aging effects and nuisance variables (age, sex, scanner protocol) between pre- and post-surgical timepoints, rather than for clinical diagnostic or prognostic applications. The normative model enables subject-wise paired analysis by predicting expected values for each individual at both timepoints and accounting for healthy aging. The study suggests future applications could include: (1) correlating structural changes with post-surgical functional outcomes (visual field impairment, cognitive/memory/language deficits); (2) investigating differences in morphological changes between seizure-free and seizure-persistent patients; (3) using morphological abnormalities for pre-surgical localization; (4) understanding mechanisms of cognitive impairment in epilepsy using independent morphological components. Authors note that regions with greatest morphological changes (orbitofrontal/inferior frontal cortex) likely reflect mechanical 'sagging' into resection cavity rather than biological reorganization. The independent measures (K, I, S) revealed additional morphological information concealed by covariance in traditional measures, particularly detecting subtle changes in K due to its near-invariant value in controls.

NONCANONICAL_DATA:
- general_notes.important_information: "IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE: While this study uses normative modeling techniques, it does NOT fit the systematic review PICO criteria for normative modeling applications to psychiatric/neurological disorders for diagnostic or clinical utility purposes. Instead, normative modeling is used as a METHODOLOGICAL TOOL to: (1) correct for healthy aging between pre- and post-surgical scans; (2) account for nuisance variables (age, sex, scanner protocol); (3) enable fair comparison of morphological changes after surgery. The primary research question is about understanding the EFFECTS OF SURGERY on brain morphology, not about using normative modeling for diagnosis, prognosis, or clinical decision-making in epilepsy. The study does not assess individual-level deviation patterns for clinical utility, diagnostic support, or patient stratification - which are the key outcomes (O in PICO) for the systematic review. Therefore, this paper may be a candidate for EXCLUSION from the systematic review despite using normative modeling techniques. The normative model serves as a baseline correction method rather than a clinical application. Dataset details: 924 healthy controls total (833 NKI + 91 site-matched). NKI subjects: 96 rejected for quality issues, 833 used for training. Site-matched controls: 22 protocol-1, 69 protocol-2. All controls processed twice (with/without temporal lobes). TLE patients: 101 total (55 left, 46 right onset), scanned with two protocols: 52 with protocol-1 (0.94×0.94×1.1mm), 49 with protocol-2 (1×1×1mm). Pre-surgical scans up to 3 years before surgery; post-surgical scans 2-13 months after surgery (median 3.6 months). Novel methodology: Independent morphological measures K (tension), I (isometric size), S (shape) derived from scaling law of cortical folding, capturing information orthogonal to traditional measures T (thickness), At (total area), Ae (exposed area). Theoretical framework: Universal scaling law Ae ∝ (At·T^0.5)^1.25, where k is relatively preserved across species but shows disease-related changes. Data availability: NKI data public at http://fcon_1000.projects.nitrc.org/indi/enhanced/. Patient data planned for public repository 2023/2024. De-identified morphological summaries on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7957831). Analysis code on GitHub (https://github.com/cnnp-lab/2023Leiberg_ATLRmorphology). Ethics: Newcastle University Ethics Committee approval 8841/2020. No pre-registration. Seizure outcomes: ILAE classification at 12 months; 23/101 patients (22.8%) had recurrent seizures (ILAE 3+): 12 left TLE, 11 right TLE."
